GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: A MachineMonster port and the batch's second seam pin. Mawler.cs:29-44: three moves all pointing at one RandomBranchState 'RAND', initial state CLAW_MOVE (moveState3, the LAST declared -- another easy inversion), and three branches added with overload #5 (`MoveRepeatType, float`), so again there is no integer argument to misread: RIP_AND_TEAR/CannotRepeat/1f, ROAR/UseOnlyOnce/1f, CLAW/CannotRepeat/1f in that ADD ORDER. mawler.py:45-47 adds rip, roar, claw with the same repeat types and the default weight 1.0, and mawler.py:51 passes claw as the initial state. `py audit/tools/state_machine_probes.py mismatch` lists Mawler among the 7 EXACT matches. guards.what: The three repeat rules -- CannotRepeat on RIP and CLAW, UseOnlyOnce on ROAR
guards.rationale: UseOnlyOnce blocks a branch iff the state is ANYWHERE in the log (RandomBranchState.cs:134-141), so ROAR is once per combat, and CannotRepeat blocks iff it is the LAST logged move (:142-157). The port passes MoveRepeatType.USE_ONLY_ONCE and .CANNOT_REPEAT through to the audited machinery rather than re-implementing them, so the rules themselves are monster_state_machine seed fact 2's `faithful` transliteration. Behaviour pinned by the pre-existing test/test_new_features.py::TestStateMachine::test_mawler_roar_used_at_most_once_per_combat (verified present by grep), and re-executed here by the 40-turn sequence diff, in which ROAR appears at most once.

guards.what: Range-bound convention on the initial-HP roll: Rng.NextInt(min, max) is max-EXCLUSIVE (Rng.cs:101-109) where Python's random.randint(a, b) INCLUDES b
guards.rationale: Checked as a convention, not just as constants. The GAME's range is [MinInitialHp, MaxInitialHp] INCLUSIVE, because Creature.SetUniqueMonsterHpValue compensates for the exclusive bound explicitly: `int num = Monster.MaxInitialHp + 1` (Creature.cs:378) feeds BOTH `Enumerable.Range(minInitialHp, num - minInitialHp)` (Creature.cs:379) and the fallback `rng.NextInt(minInitialHp, num)` (Creature.cs:383). The sim's parity port matches on both arms: `candidates = [v for v in range(lo, hi + 1) ...]` picked with `niche.next_int_range(0, len(candidates))`, fallback `niche.next_int_range(lo, hi + 1)` (combat.py:224-243), and `next_int_range` is itself max-exclusive (rng.py:182-186) -- so the two `+ 1`s land exactly where C# puts them. This unit's MaxInitialHp is `=> MinInitialHp`, so the range is the single value 72 and no endpoint can be lost; the check is recorded anyway because an off-by-one would turn a one-element candidate list into an empty one and change which ARM of SetUniqueMonsterHpValue runs (NextItem vs NextInt), which is a stream-position difference even when the HP is identical. Executed (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py hprange`, 400 seeded combats per unit): declared [72,72], observed [72,72], and the observed set is exactly the full inclusive range, so the top endpoint 72 does occur. All 15 units of this batch pass. NOTE the legacy (non-parity) path is also right by a different route: Monster.__init__'s `rng.randint(self.min_hp, self.max_hp)` (monsters/base.py:78) is inclusive on both ends, matching the game's inclusive range, and in parity mode it is overwritten before anything reads it. Rule 7: Creature.cs, Rng.cs, sts2_rl/combat.py and sts2_rl/rng.py are hashed in extra_sources.
